decision: routed to figure-it-out with a 6-PR stack plan
why: greenfield app with no grilling, large and cross-cutting

decision: chose Vite + TS + three.js over Next.js
why: fully client-side app, static deploy to GitHub Pages, no server needs

decision: architect skipped
why: shape fixed by approved mock and the Data shapes section of the plan

decision: test against fixtures built from shallow clones, not live API
why: api.github.com is blocked from this sandbox; git clone of public repos works

decision: tree height linear in log10(files): 1 at one file, 3.8 from 100k; whole skeleton scaled so trunk and spread follow
why: owner asked more files = bigger tree; log keeps 36 files readable and 97k on the island
evidence: src/grow/size.ts; dotfiles 2.20/1.17, vite 3.11/2.05, linux 3.99/2.41 height/reach at island radius 2

decision: island radius fixed (2) for every repo, still seeded per repo for shape
why: size differences only read against a constant reference

decision: camera frames the stage (tallest tree on the island), not the tree on show; desktop reserves side column and a typical title width
why: per-tree framing cancels size differences; panel content would otherwise change the scale

decision: pinned folder zoom floor follows the tree on show (capped at the stage), not the stage
why: with the stage floor a sapling folder barely zoomed in; keeps pre-change pin zoom

decision: spin fps comparison inconclusive; triangles equal (16.8k vs 16.5k)
why: shared 4-core box at load 6-18 with other agents; base runs ranged 9.6-16.2 fps, after 9.4-10.6

decision: traced load and spin with scripts/trace.mjs, 5 runs each
why: playbook step 1: attribute long tasks to call stacks before fixing
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/baseline/summary.json; medians longest dotfiles-low 310, linux-low 276, vite-low 355, vite-high 341 ms; spin 41.0/26.8/27.2/9.8 fps
result: every load task over 50 ms is a sync wait on the GPU process: GPU context creation (2D canvas for the contact texture, then WebGL getContext), and shader links at the first frame and at the first tree frame; spin is GPU-process bound (CrGpuMain 97-99% busy, renderer main 10-14%)

decision: draw the contact-shadow gradient into a DataTexture instead of a 2D canvas
why: mantra 1 (don't do it): the 2D canvas started a second GPU context, CommandBufferProxyImpl::Initialize 127-189 ms inside the startup task
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/f1/summary.json vs baseline, 5 runs each: startup task 296->244 ms dotfiles, 277->278 linux; sum of tasks over 50 ms 655->469 dotfiles, 607->459 linux; canvas pixel diff max 1/255 at low and high
result: kept: about 150 ms less blocking per load; context creation cost moved to getContext, so the longest task barely moves

decision: compile every program at startup with compileAsync and hold frames until a fence passes
why: mantra 5 (when they're not looking): link programs while the worker grows the tree
result: rejected: SwiftShader has no KHR_parallel_shader_compile, the fence passes before ANGLE finishes linking, so the first draw waited on every program at once; compiling during generation also competes with the worker for the 4 CPU cores

decision: same, but query one program per task so each wait covers one link
why: split the link waits under 100 ms each
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/f2b/summary.json: longest 706 dotfiles, 872 linux; first query waits 690-790 ms
result: rejected: the command buffer is FIFO, so the first query waits for every compile queued before it, and single SwiftShader links still take 100-260 ms

decision: rebased onto main with the island and tree sizes; re-measured spin with GPU-process CPU per frame
why: wall-clock fps swings 2x on the shared sandbox, CPU per frame does not
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/abl/linux-low-2.txt (runtime ablation, one page, 3 rounds): 154 ms/frame; nothing drawn 60; labels hidden 132; sky hidden 114 (earlier run); UI hidden 125
result: the island added fill; sky quad, labels and tree each cost 20-30 ms of GPU-process CPU per frame

decision: paint the sky as the container's CSS gradient behind a transparent canvas; the sky quad draws only into PNG snapshots
why: mantra 1 (don't do it): the full-screen sky pass filled every pixel on the software GL each frame, while the browser rasters a CSS gradient once
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/ab-stem.tsv, linux low, 3 interleaved runs: 158 -> 140 ms/frame GPU-process CPU, 23.0 -> 25.8 fps; screenshots scratchpad/pr7/shots/*: at most 0.016% of pixels differ, all at label edges

decision: draw each label stem as its own element stretched by transform instead of a pill pseudo-element sized by a custom property
why: mantra 1: resizing the stem inside the pill repainted the pill every spin frame
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/ab-stem.tsv, linux low, 3 interleaved runs: 140 -> 132 ms/frame, 25.8 -> 27.8 fps

decision: link the tree and island programs one per task at startup from stand-in meshes
why: mantra 5: link while the worker grows the tree
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/ab-warm.tsv, 4 runs: longest 561 -> 1028 ms linux low, 559 -> 1008 dotfiles low; the first link query after startup waits about 1 s
result: rejected: same FIFO wait the 2026-11-03 compileAsync attempt hit

decision: hold the cover, bark and leaves back one frame each on the first tree, so a frame links at most one new program
why: mantra 3 (do it less at once); a growing tree starts collapsed, so the hold does not show
evidence: scratchpad/pr7/ab-stage.tsv, 4 interleaved runs: longest 889 -> 492 ms linux low, 862 -> 476 dotfiles low
result: kept; each link still takes 300-600 ms on SwiftShader, so the 100 ms target is out of reach while GL runs on the main thread

decision: new run for PR 12 (CI weather); rows before this one are from earlier runs
why: decision log is shared across PRs

decision: weather thresholds over the last 20 finished runs: storm at 3 failures in a row from the newest; rain when the newest failed or at least 3 failures that are half the runs; cloudy for any other failure; sunny when all passed; clear when none
why: owner asked for sunny/partly cloudy/rain/storm/no CI; a streak reads as broken now, scattered failures as flaky

decision: ask the API for status=completed as well as branch and per_page=20, and count only success vs failure/timed_out/startup_failure
why: in-progress runs would otherwise crowd out finished ones; cancelled and skipped runs say nothing about health

decision: a 404 from the runs endpoint is no CI (clear sky); 403, 429, other errors and the network mean no weather and no chip
why: the tree already proved the repo exists, so 404 means Actions is off; weather must never become an error screen

decision: worker posts the branch as soon as it knows it (cache hit or repo info) so the runs request starts beside the tree download; samples and links with a branch start at once
why: parallel with the tree without a second repo-info request against the 60/hour limit

decision: clouds, sun and lightning hang on a backdrop fixed to the camera 60 units out, behind the tree; rain and snow fall in world space around the island and stop on it
why: owner said never hide the tree behind clouds; a world-space ring of clouds would sit in front of it at some spin angles

decision: weather moves in vertex shaders from one time uniform; moving weather renders every frame like spin, no 30 fps cap
why: a half-rate cap would read as 30 fps in auto quality's 2 s check and step quality down with spin off; spin already renders every frame by default

decision: reduced motion freezes weather at a fixed time with no lightning; tab hidden relies on requestAnimationFrame pausing
why: flashes are a photosensitivity risk; rAF already stops in hidden tabs and dt is capped at 0.1 s on return

decision: weather setting is not in share links; wx= is a preview param that the setting overrides
why: share links carry palette and colorBy only, not ground/spin/labels; turning weather off should be absolute

decision: sample runs are hand-written: vite 20 green runs (sunny), dotfiles and linux no runs (clear); make-runs.mjs added to regenerate them
why: api.github.com is blocked in this sandbox; dotfiles and linux have no .github/workflows in their sample trees

decision: clouds rebuilt smaller and rounder (icosahedron detail 1, softer shading) after first screenshots read as crumpled rocks
why: first pass looked like boulders, not clouds

decision: snow drew nothing; rewrote the snow branch of the fall vertex shader as a plain if and fixed a reversed smoothstep
why: winter storm screenshot showed no flakes while uSnow=0 drew quads
